Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the third and final session of Day 4. The English players are in a huddle, before they spread out on the field. The openers for New Zealand, Tom Latham and Devon Conway make their way out. As expected, James Anderson will begin with the ball.
... Day 4, Session 3 ...

Right then. New Zealand have a lead of 103 runs and will be looking to increase that when they come out to bat, in the third session. It does not seem like there will be a result to this game, with only one day remaining after play today, but the hosts will want to come out and make a statement with the ball. Join us for the third and final session of the day shortly.

This has been a very good bowling display by the visitors and especially by the veteran, Tim Southee, as he came, he saw and he conquered, as he grabbed 6 wickets to his name and ran through the middle order of the English Lions. Jamieson supported his partner-in-crime well as he finished with 3 to his name. Wagner had a solitary wicket as well. New Zealand bowled well for the most parts but would have wanted to wrap things up quickly, which they were not able to do. Nevertheless, they will be happy with their bowling show.

Apart from Rory Burns and Joe Root, none of the English batters really stepped up to the plate. England lost 2 quick wickets before Tea, on Day 2 and were on the back foot, but the duo of Root and Burns stitched a 93-run stand and kept England afloat. But when Root lost his wicket, England completely derailed and let the Kiwis dominate proceedings. Burns continued on and Ollie Robinson proved to be a successful partner, as he got to 42, but ended up losing his wicket. After that, Burns notched up his 100 and played some lusty strokes to finish on 132, before he fell and the hosts ended their innings on 275.

This has been a brilliant bowling display by the Kiwis, but they will be slightly disappointed that they could not close the innings out early! Yes, they were behind the 8-ball when the duo of Burns and Root were going about their business, but when Southee got rid of Root on the very first ball on Day 4, the batting of the hosts crumbled, apart from the resilience shown by Burns and the debutant, Ollie Robinson towards the end.

OUT! EDGED AND CAUGHT! Southee comes back and ends England's innings and he ends with 6 snares to his name. A good length delivery outside off, the ball seams away enough as Burns looks to drive this one through the covers, but the ball takes the outside edge and it is gobbled up by BJ Watling. ENGLAND FINISH ON 275 AND NOW IT IS TIME FOR TEA!
Commentary.Howout: c BJ Watling b Tim Southee

Commentary.Commentary: Tim Southee is back into the attack. He replaces Neil Wagner.

The fielder chases the ball and Burns comes back for the second. Fabulous knock under pressure. He gets to his century. What a knock. He will remember this for ages.

Review time! Kane Williamson takes the review, towards the end of the timer, for this LBW shout. Let's see what the replays say.
Neil Wagner is called back to bowl, by Kane Williamson. 18-3-53-0 for him so far.

Commentary.Howout: c BJ Watling b Kyle Jamieson

Outside off, Wood lets it sail through.

DRINKS! As the physio has a look at Burns, the umpires decide to take a drinks break. After a flurry of wickets fell, England found some light, when Burns and Robinson stitched a good stand and helped restore some parity. But, Southee came and disrupted their momentum and removed Robinson. Now, England will be piling their hopes on Burns to score his century and cut the deficit even further. The Kiwis will be banking on Southee and Jamieson to cause some damage with the new ball and wrap up England's innings.
Mark Wood is the next man in for the hosts.

OUT! CAUGHT! Southee bags a fifer and Robinson's watch comes to a close. Pitches it short on middle, Robinson went for the pull but did not get the elevation there and only managed to get a top edge. The ball was in the air for a long time but Kyle Jamieson at fine leg grabs a fantastic catch. Robinson, who was looking really good has to depart for a well-made 42. Southee is delighted. This is Southee's 12th 5-wicket haul and his 2nd at Lord's. England slip further now.
Commentary.Howout: c Kyle Jamieson b Tim Southee

A touch fuller on off, defended off the back foot. THAT WILL BE LUNCH ON DAY 4!

England know that they need to pull their socks up as they are behind by 214 runs and with the exception of Burns, who is out in the middle, they do not have a lot of batting talent lined up. The hosts will be hoping that they can rely on the likes of Burns, mainly, and the remaining batters to ensure that the deficit is cut down to a large extent. Will the hosts bat well in the second session or will the Kiwis continue their bowling exploits? All the answers in the second session. Join us for the same shortly.
Tossed up on middle, defended on the leg side watchfully.

What a morning the Kiwis have had here! With the entirety of Day 3 being washed out, they would have wanted to come out and make huge strides in this game and they have done just that. Right from ball one of the day, the Black Caps have dominated proceedings and have pushed England on the back foot. As soon as Joe Root was sent packing on ball one, England failed to get going. They were at 139/3 and just in a span of a couple of overs, they fell to 140/6. Southee has been their gun bowler and has snared 3 to his name, whereas, Jamieson has got one.
Fuller on off, worked towards mid-wicket.

The Kiwis appeal for a catch and the umpire raises his finger. Ollie straightaway reviews. Ultra edge confirms that there was no bat involved. The decision will get overturned and Robinson will stay at the crease.

The next batsman to come in at No.8 is Ollie Robinson.

OUT! TIMBER! WOW! What a morning New Zealand are having! The debutant heads back for a duck and the Black Caps are bowling with fire and venom. Southee strikes again and the visitors are on top. A good length ball, around off, but the ball seams back in sharply as James Bracey looks to drive this one. Bracey misses and the ball sneaks in between the bat and pad and the off stump goes for a walk. Brilliant, brilliant work from Southee and he will be looking for a fifer now.

DRINKS! Just the start to the day that the visitors would have been looking for. They have removed 3 English batters and are bowling the right lines and lengths, which is making batting difficult for the hosts. Southee and Jamieson have been on fire and the Black Caps will be looking to take some more wickets before Lunch. The hosts, whereas, would want Bracey and Burns to see off the challenge until Lunch, atleast.

Fuller outside off, the ball kept low, Burns leaves it alone.
Outside off, left alone by Burns.

Similar line and length. Similar result as the previous one.
Starts with a length delivery, outside off, Burns shoulders arms to that one.
First change in bowling on Day 4. Colin de Grandhomme is handed the ball now. 9-3-12-0 so far.
Outside off, Bracey keeps it out.

Outside off, Bracey watches the ball sail through.

The debutant, James Bracey strides out into the middle now.

OUT! CAUGHT! Southee strikes with another and the English batting line-up seems to be in a hurry to head back to the shed. Pitches it full and outside off, the ball was angling away from the batsman. Lawrence looks to drive but gets a thick outside edge. The ball flies to Colin de Grandhomme at the third slip who takes the catch with ease. Lawrence has to take the long walk back. He departs early and New Zealand is ruling this game currently.
Commentary.Howout: c Colin de Grandhomme b Tim Southee

OUT! LBW! Brilliant bowling from Southee and a great decision by Williamson to take the review, as it results in a wicket. The Kiwis strike again and Pope's stay comes to a close. Good length delivery on middle and off, at 130kph, angling in, Pope is late into his shot and misses. The ball gets hit on the front pad. The Kiwis appeal for a possible LBW but the umpire nods his head. Williamson straightaway signals 'T' and it is sent upstairs. The Ultra Edge confirms there is no bat involved. Ball Tracking confirms the three reds and the on-field decision has been overturned. Pope was looking in good touch but he has to depart. England lose two early wickets into the session and it will worry them.
Dan Lawrence is the new batter in for the English Lions!

Review time! Kane Williamson does not wait for the timer to go off, as he signals the 'T' and seems confident that this LBW should, will result in a wicket. Ultra Edge shows no bat involved. Ball Tracker rolls in and it is THREE REDS! The on-field decision has been overturned and Pope heads back to the shed!

OUT! CAUGHT! Sensational start to Day 4 and the English skipper has to head back on his very first delivery. A good length delivery on off, seaming away, Root stays back at the crease and looks to defend. The ball zips past the bat and finds the outside edge. The ball carries through to Ross Taylor at first slip and he gets low and takes the catch. Taylor feels that he has taken the catch but he is not a hundred percent sure. The umpires converge and decide to take this one upstairs, with their soft signal being out. Replays roll in and it is seen that Taylor's hands are underneath the ball as he takes the catch and the big screen shows out. A wicket off the first delivery and Joe Root has to depart. Just the start that the Kiwis would have been envisioning.
Commentary.Howout: c Ross Taylor b Kyle Jamieson

Commentary.Commentary: Who comes out next for England? It is Ollie Pope!

Is that a clean catch? Ross Taylor feels as though he has taken it cleanly, but he is not completely sure and so, the umpires want to make sure. Their soft signal is out too. Replays show that his hands are underneath the ball and the big screen reads OUT!

Ready for all the action to begin now. The batters for England, Joe Root and Rory Burns make their way out into the middle now. Kyle Jamieson will begin proceedings with the ball for the Kiwis. Here he comes...

Hello and a warm welcome to the fourth day of the first Test between England and New Zealand. The Kiwis couldn't have asked for a better start on Day 2 as they got two early wickets and ensured that the hosts remain under pressure. However, Burns and Root's intact partnership ensured that they are not out of the game. While Day 3 was completely washed out, Day 4 would be an interesting one as the Kiwi pacers will be looking to bundle the English batters out, before they take the lead. With the weather playing games with our heart on Day 3, we will all be hoping that we have a rain-free day of cricket ahead of us. Will the Kiwis be able to take control of this Test? Only time will tell. Join us for what is going to be an interesting battle on Day 4.
... Day 4, Session 1 ...

Right then! Unfortunately, we did not have any action on Day 3. Let us hope that we get some good action on Day 4 and Day 5. 98 overs are scheduled to be bowled on Day 4 and Day 5. Join us on 5th June 2021 as the play will being on 1100 local (1000 GMT), but like always our build-up will begin before that. Till then, stay safe and take care!

Update 1635 local (1535 GMT) - Well, this was coming. After all the rain that we have had on Day 3, the umpires have decided to call it off. It is Stumps on Day 3! It promised to be a great day of cricket but unfortunately, the rain gods had different plans. It rained throughout the day and play wasn't possible. Coming back to the game, with rain washing out the entire Day 3, it would take some dramatic collapse by either of these teams for there to be a result in this game.

Update 1630 local (1530 GMT) - The umpires are out there having a look at the conditions but they still have their umbrellas up. The groundstaff are out there working too. It looks like it is still raining.

Update 1600 local (1500 GMT) - It has gotten brighter out in the middle but there is a bit of drizzle still. We are hearing that the latest we can start is by 1800 local (1700 GMT) and play can go on till 1930 local but it has to stop raining first and it also depends on how long the groundsmen will take to make the field ready for play. Stay with us.
... Day 3, Session 3 ...

Update 1540 local (1440 GMT) - Tea has been taken and we have still not gotten any play yet on Day 3. It is raining but it has gotten a little brighter. Will we get any play on Day 3? The drainage here is brilliant but for that, the rain has to stop first. Stay tuned.

Update 1524 local (1424 GMT) - I am afraid that there is nothing to update as it is still raining and the covers are firmly on the pitch. This session is also certain to get washed out and we can only hope that it stops raining and we get some play on Day 3. Stay with us.

Update 1434 local (1334 GMT) - Unfortunately we still do not have any good news for you. It is still raining at Lord's and the covers are still there. Yup, it has been that kind of a day. Stay tuned for more as we hope that we get some cricket today.

Update 1347 local (1247 GMT) - The scheduled Lunch might be over, but unfortunately it still continues to pour down at Lord's. We hope for the rain to stop so that play can resume soon. Till then, we wait and watch. Stay tuned for more updates.
... Day 3, Session 2 ...

Update 1300 local (1200 GMT) - Lunch has been taken on Day 3! Unfortunately, we did not get to see any play in the first session of Day 3 as rain continues to fall in London. The conditions do not seem to improve as well and it seems like it is going to be a long wait. All we can hope for is that the rain stops quickly and play gets underway sooner than later. Stay with us as we bring you all the updates.

Update 1230 local (1130 GMT) - The rain has not stopped and it looks like it is going to be a long wait. We are hearing that Lunch will be taken at 1300 local (1200 GMT). Let's hope that the rain subsides and we get play as soon as possible. Stay with us.

Update 1152 local (1052 GMT) - There is still no improvement in conditions and the rain has settled in. The drainage here is very good but for that, the rain has to stop. It looks like the first session will be washed out. Let's keep our fingers crossed though. Stay with us.

Update 1136 local (1036 GMT) - We are still playing the waiting game as the rain has not stopped yet and the covers are firmly on. It does not look like the play will resume anytime soon. Let's stay hopeful though. Stay tuned.

Update 1100 local (1000 GMT) - It is still raining in London and we are certainly not starting on time. It looks grim at the moment. Let's start positive though and keep our fingers crossed that we get some play soon. Stay with us.

Update 1006 local (0906 GMT) - Not the greatest of news to start off with as it is currently raining in London and the covers are on. It looks like we will have a delayed start to Day 3. Nothing has been confirmed yet. Let's hope that the rain clears soon and we get play as soon as possible. Stay tuned for further updates.

Hello and a warm welcome to Day 3 of the Test between England and New Zealand. Dare I say that the team which does better on this day will have a lot of advantage in the game. The game is nicely poised with Root and Burns still batting well for England, the plan for them is to bat as long as possible to get close to the New Zealand total. For New Zealand, it will be crucial to break this stand and then pick quick wickets to bundle out the hosts. Who will this day belong to? We will find out. Stay tuned for more updates.
... Day 3, Session 1 ...

Right then! That's all from Day 2 of the first Test match between England and New Zealand. England will be pretty happy with how the day went and they will look to continue the good work on Day 3 while New Zealand will need to bowl much better than they have on Day 2. Day 3 will begin on 4th June 2021 at 1100 local (1000 GMT). Join us then. Cheers and take care.

New Zealand will be slightly disappointed! They had the advantage after picking up two wickets pretty quickly but they have not made use of it at all. They tried hard but they bowled too many freebies and they were punished. Southee was the pick of the bowlers while Jamieson too was decent. But, Wagner was slightly disappointing as his tactics of bowling short deliveries did not work and was played quite easily by Burns and Root.

England started slowly after Tea but after they got set, runs were coming pretty quickly. Both Burns and Root have played very well so far and are looking in ominous touch. Burns has reached a wonderful fifty and will look to score a big one on Day 3 while the skipper Root is also looking in sublime form. But their job is not done yet and they have a lot of work to do on Day 3. They will be pleased though to not lose more than 2 wickets.

An excellent day's play comes to an end and it will be England who will be the happier of the two sides at the end of it. England were in trouble at the start of the final session but Root and Burns have done well to weather the storm and go unscathed. New Zealand will be disappointed that they could not make use of the advantage after picking up two early wickets.

Drinks! England have done well so far in this session. They have not lost a wicket in this session so far and both Burns and Root are looking very good out in the middle. They need to continue and make sure that they bat as long as possible. New Zealand, on the other hand, would hope that they pick up a few more wickets before Stumps on Day 2. Let's see how it pans out.

.... Day 2, Session 3 ...

New Zealand, on the other hand, have been brilliant with the ball so far. Both Southee and Jamieson have been right on the money and they have bowled tight lines and lengths. Southee especially has done a very good job and picked up Crawley with a peach of a delivery but Jamieson too has done a good job. They will look to continue doing the same in the final session and prize out a few more wickets. Join us at 1530 local (1430 GMT) for the final session of Day 2.

England needed a good start but they did not get that as they lost Sibley for a duck and lost Crawley soon after. Burns has looked very good at the middle but he needs to continue and post a big one on the board. Root has joined him in the middle and has gotten off to a start. They still trail by 353 runs but their first aim would be to play out till Stumps without many wickets falling.

End of an exhilarating session but one would feel that New Zealand have taken this session. After getting bowled out for 378 with Conway reaching a double century, they have managed to pick up two wickets and have put themselves on the front foot. England will be disappointed that they have lost two wickets and they have a very long way to go.
